purpose: Source-location registry for systematic Australian political evidence acquisition. A listed site or endpoint is a research location, not evidence by itself.
rules: Prefer parliament, electoral authority, government and official party sources for primary political facts and attributed claims.
Preserve source URL, source snapshot ID and genuine capture time for evidence actually ingested.
A site listing is not evidence by itself.
A raw source change is not a political signal; semantic promotion requires the configured review path.
Party and government claims remain attributed to their publisher unless independently verified.
Observation remains distinct from inference and no projection effect occurs without registered evidence lineage.
Jurisdictions remain distinct; cross-jurisdiction effects require explicit evidence rather than assumed transfer.
Current parliamentary, electoral, government and party publication surfaces change on different clocks and remain separate research targets.
Structured publication additions may enter deterministic review, but publication does not verify the underlying claim content.
Contradictions remain visible until evidence resolves them; resolution must preserve the original claims and identify the resolving evidence.
Historical material may support context and reconstruction, but forward-state claims require contemporaneous forward capture.
No source is silently substituted for another jurisdiction, publisher or evidentiary class.
